captions.linkedin:
Good research includes the downside.

McKinsey's 2019 report, "Modular construction: From projects to products", found that modular construction can be 20-50% faster than traditional building and can save up to 20% on cost. It also warned of potential losses of up to 10% if delivery or material costs spike.

The difference comes from where the work happens: in a factory, conditions are controlled and processes repeat.

Four questions I'd ask before choosing prefab: What does it save in time? What does it cost? What are the delivery risks? Who is responsible for quality?
